text:
oncall-bot: Alert: private-vpn healthcheck failures reported for customer AcmeHealth (eu-west-1). 3000s window, 30% packet loss :warning:

mia: Customer reporting 502s from Private control plane and API timeouts since ~06:40 UTC. They say their services in VPC lose connectivity to our private endpoint intermittently.

samir: Can you grab the customer-side ipsec logs and our tunnel metrics? My gut: DPD/SA renegotiation flapping. Seen this pattern with lifetime mismatch + NAT-T.

mia: Pasted customer debug (redacted):
```
May 12 06:39:58 ipsec[1234]: IKEv2: CHILD_SA rekeying failed, retransmit
May 12 06:40:01 ipsec[1234]: IKEv2 DPD timeout, sending DELETE
May 12 06:40:01 ipsec[1234]: peer 203.0.113.42: IKE_SA state destroyed
```

charlie-net: From our side counters: spikes in tx drops on tunnel ENI 10.2.0.0/24, and our VPN gateway logged frequent `no response to DPD` events.

alex: Customer traceroute shows path reaches their CPE then stops, intermittent `* * *`. ping to our control plane 10.18.11.5 shows 40% loss during window.

kevin-support: Customer says they applied a config push earlier today to their firewall (changed IKE lifetimes and enabled aggressive rekey). They may have set SA lifetime to 6h while our default 8h.

samir: That mismatch will cause one side to rekey earlier -> simultaneous rekey and potential transient traffic drop if rekey messages lost. Also check DPD timers: if their DPD is shorter than retrans threshold we delete SA prematurely.

charlie-net: Can we see IKE proposals and NAT-T presence? If traffic is behind NAT they must use UDP/4500. If firewall blocks 4500 responses DPD won't recover.

mia: Customer confirms NAT on CPE and they allowed UDP/500 but not UDP/4500. They thought UDP/500 was enough.

alex: That would explain it. When NAT-T kicks in we need UDP/4500 for encapsulated ESP. Without it rekey messes up.

samir: Quick mitigation options:
- Ask customer to allow UDP/4500 both directions.
- Align SA lifetimes (we can temporarily lower our lifetime to 6h to match their change).
- Increase DPD timeout on our gateway to tolerate transient misses.

kevin-support: I proposed a short maintenance window to test opening 4500 on their firewall. Customer agreed to try config change and perform controlled rekey.

eng-infra: We can push a temporary config on the gateway: set ike_lifetime=21600 (6h), dpd_action=restart, dpd_interval=30, dpd_timeout=180. Will schedule a deploy in 10 minutes if we get go-ahead.

mia: Customer ready. They will open UDP/4500 and revert their aggressive rekey after test. They will also run a continuous ping to our endpoint during the window.

charlie-net: Added network capture rule to collect ESP plain/encap attempts and IKE handshakes during the window. Will attach pcaps after.

(5 minutes later)
oncall-bot: Deploy started: temporary gateway config for customer AcmeHealth by eng-infra (deploy-id: deploy-9023).

kevin-support: Customer opened UDP/4500. Running `tcpdump -n host 203.0.113.42 and port 4500` shows traffic now. No more DPD DELETE events in last 2 mins. :thumbsup:

samir: Great — still want them to revert mismatched lifetimes. If they keep a shorter lifetime it's a recurring risk. Recommend aligning to our defaults or coordinate planned rekeys.

mia: Customer reports API errors dropped to zero and pings stable. They will keep UDP/4500 allowed.

eng-infra: Rolling back temporary lifetime change to avoid config drift. We'll instead add a note in rollout docs: always open UDP/4500 for NAT'd CPEs and coordinate SA lifetime changes.

alex: Can we create a short KB for support referencing DPD + NAT-T issues for Private customers? I'll draft.

kevin-support: Filed ticket ACME-2307 with summary and steps taken, attached pcaps and ipsec logs. Marking as resolved once customer confirms 24h stability.

mia: Customer will monitor. Thanks team. :sparkles:
